blindSummary: This country's risk profile was set by its own courts: unlike the decriminalised neighbouring states in its region, its high court upheld the "buggery" and gross-indecency laws in 2024, so criminalisation (up to 10 years) remains formally in force. Enforcement is rare, but the legal floor and judicial hostility distinguish it from the region's decriminalised neighbours.
blindOutOfScope: 2024 ruling upheld criminalisation — opposite trajectory from neighbours.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying page from an international legal-aid trust documents constitutional challenges to criminalisation across this country's region; this country retains colonial-era buggery and gross-indecency laws.
NOTE: the underlying rights-group article concerns a neighbouring state's 2022 ruling, not this country specifically; included as regional context.

LGBT travel-news archive (Sept 2012): homosexuality is illegal in this country, stigmatised and not tolerated; there is no LGBT organisation here (unlike in one neighbouring state); most LGBT people marry opposite-sex spouses or live discreetly; a regional HIV/AIDS alliance bridges the gap indirectly.

LGBT news outlet (Feb 2024): this country's high court upheld the ban on gay sex - two provisions of the 1988 criminal code remain in force (up to 10 years for anal intercourse; 5 years for 'gross indecency'); the challenge by two named claimants, who said they were forced to leave the country, was rejected; the presiding judge found the laws 'reasonably required'.
International human-rights organisation report (July 2023), titled in effect that LGBT people here face bias: documents discrimination and violence against LGBT residents ahead of the court ruling.

Regional LGBT advocacy alliance's press release (Feb 2024): the high-court ruling undermines the rights of LGBTQ+ people in this country - the dismissal of the challenge to the two criminal-code provisions was said to weaponise hate by sanctioning it at the highest court level (a criticism echoed by a local LGBT group); the attorney general was joined by religious groups as interested parties; the release says the ruling legitimises violence and abuses.
blindTangential: The buggery laws (10 years, upheld 2024) remain a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
